failure_summary.description: Agents missed an accepted preference, refinement, or earlier requested domain when interpreting the latest turn.
Search or filter results were not consistently assigned and saved to cache.
Agents sought unnecessary clarification or supplied unsupported defaults for missing or unusual dates.
A minimum hotel rating was encoded without the range's upper bound.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly requires assigning and saving tool results and checking mandatory inputs, so repeating those rules would not address a skill gap. The missing clarification is how to interpret elliptical replies and preserve the scope of earlier requests; the added instruction targets that recurring omission.

edits.content: - Before planning, interpret the latest reply in light of the preceding assistant prompt and the full conversation. A brief affirmative (such as “yes” or “that sounds great”) accepts the specific action or preference offered; carry forward any values supplied with it, and keep earlier requested domains in scope. Map accepted amenities, locations, or proximity requests to supported criteria and re-check cache coverage. Do not treat an affirmative reply as a no-op or ask again for information already provided.
